name: Caterer

pf.license.need: Always for food: a food service permit for the kitchen the food is made in, from the health department. Bar service: a liquor license, or a caterer's permit, where the state's rules require one. All from the state form.
pf.license.per event: Where the state's rules require it, a permit for each event with a bar, or for food served at a temporary event. Filed by the business before the date the rules set.
pf.license.who holds it: The business holds the kitchen's food permit, any liquor license and any event permits. Each person holds their own card: a food handler card for cooks, a server training card for bartenders, where the state's rules require one.
pf.license.manager on site: A certified food protection manager is in charge at every event and at the kitchen, where the state's rules require one.
what to ask: The kitchen's food service permit number
The liquor license number, if the business pours drinks
Each cook's food handler card and each bartender's server card, in their invite reply
The food protection manager certificate, and who holds it
pf.license.how it's checked: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks going live: No food service permit on file: catering stays offline. No liquor license: the bar services stay hidden. A bartender without a current card is never offered for a bar.
pf.license.renewals: A reminder 30 days before a permit, card or certificate runs out. Once one lapses, the services it covers pause.
pf.license.insurance or bond: Liability insurance, and liquor liability insurance for a bar, on file with end dates. Many venues ask for a certificate naming them.
pf.license.background checks: Only where the state's form asks.

pf.visit.check-in at the customer's place: The check-in code, given to the lead chef on arrival. A planner or a day-of contact can get the code instead, when a mobile is given for them.
pf.visit.check-in at the kitchen: The code at the counter for a pickup or a tasting, or the chef types it.
pf.visit.delivery and setup: Every order is delivered and set up. The customer checks it and signs for it, with a photo of the setup and the food labels.
pf.visit.food safety on the day: Hot food stays hot and cold food stays cold. Food out of temperature control is marked with its time limit (the federal model food code says 4 hours) and is served or thrown away by then.
pf.visit.bar: Guests 21 and over only, with ID. A guest with no ID gets a mocktail. A guest who is visibly drunk is not served, and the lead chef tells the host.
pf.visit.allergies: Allergy plates go out first, labeled by seat, checked by the food protection manager against the secure page.
pf.visit.work changes at the event: More guests, extra food or extra service time only with the customer's written yes by text, at the rate shown before booking. No yes in 10 minutes: service ends on time.
pf.visit.proof it's done: The lead chef texts DONE once the food is set up and checked, or served and cleared for a full-service event.

roles: Bartender (a current card where the state requires one)
pf.staff.supervision: A certified food protection manager is in charge at each event and at the kitchen, where the state's rules require one.
pf.staff.who OKs what: The owner OKs every wedding, every quote over the limit, every guest count change over 10%, and any stand-in lead.
pf.staff.stand-ins: A lead chef the owner trusts, even from outside the team, only if the customer agrees. A bartender only with a current card.
pf.staff.who does what (the example): Remy makes grazing boards and prices event menus at the menu consult; Sasha does every other kitchen service. Rowan leads quoted events; Emery does hot breakfasts and boxed lunches.

pf.rules.written contract: The business's own contract, filled in from the booking, signed by every customer named and the business before money is taken, for every quoted event. Any parts the state's rules add come from the state form.
pf.rules.date hold: An event date stays saved while the contract is signed: up to 24 hours here, and longer for a wedding (the owner's setting).
pf.rules.events a day: The kitchen's own limit of events a day (the owner's setting).
pf.rules.final count: Due before the event, on the day the owner sets. It sets the rest paid on the bill after the event. Over 10% more needs the owner's OK.
pf.rules.cancel schedule: Free to cancel for a set time after signing. After that, a dated schedule from the contract. One free date change, if the kitchen has room (the owner's setting).
pf.rules.alcohol: Only under the business's liquor license and any event permit the state's rules require. No outside alcohol where the license forbids it.
pf.rules.records: Contracts, permits and payments kept 7 years, as for every kind of work. Allergy notes deleted the day after the event.

pf.edges.all: Every edge case is handled the general way. These matter most for catering:
catering: The guest count changes: a new price to sign; over 10% needs the owner's OK
The final count isn't in by its day: the contract's count is billed, and the owner calls about allergies
Rain or heat on an outdoor event: the weather plan in the contract
A bar permit isn't issued in time: the bar comes off, and the owner calls
The lead chef can't come: a trusted stand-in if the customer agrees, or a full refund
The customer moves the date: one free move, if the kitchen has room
The customer cancels: only what the dated schedule says is kept, with the owner's OK
A guest with no ID, or visibly drunk: no alcohol for them
An allergy plate: made apart, labeled, and checked against the secure page
The van runs late: the customer hears only if the serving time changes
Food out too long: thrown away at its time limit

Refit Oct 27 (REDESIGN 2 master): old words ops and ops on removed steps dropped; trade `more` lines kept (permits, allergies only on the secure page, pickups, food safety, the bar); facts firststeps, forms, documents, extrawork; settings arrive A setstart, B window, cutoff A 24 hours before, B 2 days before; amounts per path with name; main paths follow the master's story (A list|card|counter: a fruit tray pickup; B list|card|bill: a hot breakfast for 10); D66: the rest of a deposit is on the saved card at the end or on the bill, never charged on a set day before the event; rename pairs re-pointed to today's words.
Pilot: started from the photographer (pattern event), as the brief suggests. Catering runs the same way on its usual side: an event quoted from the customer's plan, a contract both sign, a deposit and the rest on a set day, and a date that can't move, with a trusted stand-in or a full refund. What the photographer lacked and this overlay adds: food (allergies only on the secure page, food left out thrown away by the food code's time limit, every order delivered and set up and signed for), a bar (IDs, no alcohol for a drunk guest), the final count (B7-x01 to B7-x03), and pickups at the kitchen.
Names: Sam Lee's main company is Lee Event Catering LLC (75 Mill St), with catering and bar service as its two kinds of work (trade names Lee Catering and Lee Bar Service). His second company is Lee's Kitchen LLC (19 Pine St), a carry-out kitchen with a pickup counter and a tasting table: the master's barbershop. Flow A's story is at the kitchen, flow B's at the main company, as in the master.
People: Remy Chen and Sasha Diaz are the kitchen's chefs (the master's Riley and Avery); Rowan Price (lead chef, also a bartender) and Emery Moore go out to events (Jordan and Casey). Gia Russo is a lead chef Sam trusts from outside the team (B7-54). Theo B. becomes Wren B., since Theo is a photographer pilot word. Customer Alex M. and owner Sam are kept.

Pickups are bookings: a catering pickup order is made ahead for a set day and time, with a count and money, so it's a visit at the kitchen with its code at the counter. Takeout off the shelf isn't booked (A3-32 'No walk-ins').
Flow B: the main story is an office breakfast for 20 at Alex's office, 300 Bay St, Thu Oct 22, set up 8 to 10am: quoted from Alex's plan at $640 (over Sam's $500, so Sam OKs it), both sign, a $160 deposit, and the $480 rest charged on the set day. The master's dates and times are kept, so the 8 to 10am window is a setup window before a 10am meeting.
Times: B4-83 keeps '1 Arrival windows' (renamed 'Setup windows': drop-off and setup orders) and '2 A set start time' (served events, like a wedding dinner); the stay, seat and no-person branches are off.
Money paths: A list|deposit|counter (main), list|card|counter, list|none|counter, list|deposit|none, list|full|none, photos|card|counter.
